data.content: # What to know as European leaders meet in Dublin to discuss Ukraine's security, and their own. Leaders from over 40 European countries are gathering in Dublin for a summit focused on the continent’s fragile security. Ireland’s Prime Minister Micheal Martin, right, and President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy at Government Buildings in Dublin, Ireland, Wednesday Nov. 11, 2026. (Cathal McNaughton/Pool Photo via AP). By Jill Lawless and Sam McNeil | AP. DUBLIN — Leaders from more than 40 European countries are gathering in Dublin on Thursday for a summit focused on the continent’s fragile security, amid a new U.S.-backed effort to revive talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war .

data.title: Ireland and Ukraine considering co-production of unmanned drones - BBC
data.content: # Ireland and Ukraine considering co-production of unmanned drones. Ireland's Taoiseach (prime minister) and the Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky have indicated that they may cooperate on the production of unmanned drones. Speaking at a press conference, Zelensky indicated a willingness to work with the Irish government in the co-production of drones. The taoiseach said work is ongoing between the two sides given Ukraine's expertise on drone technology and that the Irish are considering agreeing a memorandum with Ukraine on the issue. Martin said unmanned drones could benefit the Republic of Ireland in terms of maritime security. A major security operation is in place in the Irish capital for the meeting of the European leaders with extensive traffic disruption and delays expected in areas from Dublin airport to the city centre. Zelensky also thanked Ireland for its "unwavering support" for Ukraine. "I'm grateful for the willingness to help Ukraine and for the support packages.
